test.name: A review of all hits of a search spawns evaluate-search-results for each of its eleven hits
test.description: Issue #3522, research/SKILL.md "Search-hit review", the all-hits form. log_017 holds eleven hits, every one with a transcript, and none is extracted in this scenario (g9gj without src_006). The router reads results/log_017.json#hits and spawns one @plugin:evaluate-search-results per hit, at most 5 per message, so eleven spawns across more than one message of the same turn, with no report between the batches. evaluate-search-results is stubbed with one canned Match, not yet extracted, and no hitRef line (see ut_research_hv3), so the offer reads "Continue with extracting the 11 Matches?". test_search_hit_review_spawns_one_agent_per_hit asserts the eleven distinct hitRefs, projectPath, target and the offer's count from the hook records. The width of 5 is not asserted: no run record says which message a spawn came from.

input.user_message: /research Evaluate all hits of log_017 for Iram Hyde.

stub_skills.response:
verdict: match
newVitalInfo: true
alreadyExtracted: false

---

This record names Iram Hyde, and its place and period fit what his tree holds, so it is labelled a Match. It holds a detail his tree does not have yet.

judge_context: This is a ROUTING test of research/SKILL.md's "Search-hit review". The spawns are asserted deterministically from the hook records (test_routes_to_expected_skill, test_search_hit_review_spawns_one_agent_per_hit): eleven evaluate-search-results spawns, one per hit of log_017, each naming projectPath, its own hitRef and a target, and a last line "Continue with extracting the 11 Matches?". You cannot see the spawns. Do not grade them.

evaluate-search-results is STUBBED with one canned return for every hit: a Match, not yet extracted, with the same two-sentence summary. Every hit therefore comes back a Match in identical words. That is the stub, not a defect of the router, and nothing is written to the project.
The spawns go out in batches of at most 5 per message, all in this one turn. A batch is not a step: reporting between batches, or stopping after the first batch with an offer, is the failure.
The router judges nothing from the hit list itself and extracts nothing in this turn: it relays each verdict and offers the extraction.

PROJECT_LIST FIRST IS REQUIRED. When no projectPath is named, the router's first call is project_list with no arguments, to find the project. Its folder answer is the live tool's real answer, not an error.
